paragraphs.dominant_move: ideal coach and cosine -> clustered baseline ranking
timeline regression -> difficulty and social correction
factor pool -> sports and country extensions
noise and comparison -> bounded stability claim
all-time coach question -> multi-factor data problem
data and factor variety -> evaluation-system need
introduction -> assumptions and factor analysis handoff

global_organization_chain: The summary sheet and execution flow state the best-coach decision, PCA factor compression, cosine ranking, time and gender adjustments, extension, sensitivity, and robustness claims.
The illustrated problem framing, question list, and contents translate a broad all-time coach comparison into factor selection, ranking, adjustment, extension, and stability work.
The introduction frames college-coach ranking as a multi-factor comparison, identifies the intended sports and genders, and announces an evaluation-system route.
The assumptions table declares representativeness, data reliability, and the role of time horizon and gender in the later adjustment models.
The paper lists twelve coach factors, standardizes them, builds a correlation matrix, extracts principal components, and interprets ability, college influence, and social influence.
The ranking model defines an ideal coach, uses cosine similarity and an adjusted form, clusters sixty coaches by Euclidean single linkage, then reports the baseline list.
The initial top-ten table is used to introduce timeline and gender differences as reasons to modify the basic similarity ranking.
The time-line module regresses active NCAA coaches on year, converts the relation into a career-average difficulty coefficient, caps the giant effect, adjusts Google searches, and reranks.
The gender module uses one-way ANOVA to select differing factors, then rescales female wins by data whitening before a final basketball ranking.
A factor pool maps shared and sport-specific fields before football, softball, baseball, and Chinese basketball coach ranking demonstrations.
Photo-backed basketball, football, and baseball tables and a U.S. regional map turn the ranking outputs into a decision-facing presentation.
The source compares rankings before and after adjustments, adds unspecified noise to the first fifteen coaches, and uses limited order stability as stability and robustness evidence.
The closing evaluation names credibility, accessibility, self-improvement, reliability, and adaptability, then admits narrow-factor and lower-ability ranking limits.
The conclusion restates the similarity, timeline, gender, transfer, and robustness claims; the references expose web and method dependencies without frozen computational inputs.
The appendix supplies original and modified rows for the sixty basketball coaches, making several transformations inspectable while leaving their full pipeline and provenance incomplete.
Only after the positive language, organization, model, result, and visual chains are complete does the final pass record notation, inference, transfer, robustness, and reproducibility warnings.

main_argument_chains.claim: A multi-factor coach comparison becomes inspectable when the factor table passes through standardization, correlation, PCA, and visible loading interpretation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the three labels only as sample-specific interpretations until factor definitions and retention choices are validated.

main_argument_chains.claim: An ideal-coach similarity ranking needs a scale-aware repair and an explicit cluster selection before its top list is interpreted.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not treat the rank as a complete ability measurement without testing the reference, scaling, linkage, and group-selection rules.

main_argument_chains.claim: A timeline correction is traceable when the active-coach series, regression, career integral, cap, social correction, and before-after ranks are all retained.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the correction as conditional until its proportionality, units, calibration, data, and uncertainty are justified.

main_argument_chains.claim: A gender transformation is interpretable only when the test design, selected factors, whitening ratio, variance target, and reranking effect remain distinct.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Variance equalization cannot by itself establish fairness or eliminate all gender-linked measurement differences.

main_argument_chains.claim: A factor pool supports transfer only after receiving-domain field mapping, data provenance, and evaluation are specified.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the displayed lists as scoped demonstrations, not evidence that the ranking model is universal across sports or countries.

main_argument_chains.claim: Adjustment and noise comparisons can support a limited stability observation when the changed fields, outputs, and untested dimensions are visible.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Expand to seeded repeated sensitivity and structural checks before using robustness as a quality claim.

warnings.warning: The visual correlation denominator has an index mismatch in its second sum; reconstruct indices before implementation.
The printed cumulative-contribution upper index is inconsistent; verify the intended retained-component sum.
The standard-deviation summand uses a different mean subscript from the stated mean.
The general Minkowski expression omits absolute values and the merge relation mixes squared and unsquared distance notation.
The printed difficulty equation divides by k after the preceding text defines D(t)=kA(t); reconcile direction and units.
The ANOVA notation uses N inconsistently and needs correct group and total-observation degrees of freedom.
Validate the whitening variance ratio and target rather than assuming a displayed variance match establishes a fair comparison.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: The source's first page states the complete decision, method, adjustment, extension, and stability route.
The flow table makes PCA, clustering, cosine ranking, time and gender corrections, extension, sensitivity, and robustness explicit.
The illustrative sports panels communicate the multi-sport best-coach objective before formulas.
The idealistic-coach graphic binds observed coach factors to the ideal-vector comparison.
The assumptions table is the source contract for representativeness, data reliability, timeline, and gender adjustments.
The visual formula block preserves standardization, correlation, and component construction.
Eigenvalues and cumulative contribution rates establish the displayed retained-component evidence.
The component loading matrix supports the named ability, college-influence, and social-influence labels.
The bar chart visually orders Z1, Z2, and Z3 influence.
The vector-angle diagram and dot-product expression define similarity and reveal the source's direction-only comparison.
The ideal coach row and vector comparison explain the baseline ranking reference.
The overlap example motivates adjusted cosine and exposes the factor transforms.
Minkowski, Euclidean, linkage, merge equations, and the cluster plot show the eligibility calculation.
The cluster-membership table records the actual grouping used before ranking.
The baseline top-ten table is the direct comparison object that triggers adjustment modules.
The active-coach scatter, fit line, R-squared label, and prediction-interval label are the timeline-regression evidence.
The difficulty line and career-average equation connect annual trend to individual correction.
The capped difficulty-adjustment plot and social coefficient define the two time-line transformations.
The before-after ranking tables reveal which timeline changes actually occur.
The p-value table is the visual gate for selecting gender-sensitive factors.
Male/female win variance and the whitening expression are shown before the transformation claim.
The post-adjustment variance display is the source's direct whitening check.
The factor-pool diagram separates shared and sport-specific fields before transfer.
Three cross-sport top-five tables expose the transfer results and a mislabeled final table.
Photo-backed basketball ranking rows keep person, tenure, wins, games, and rate together.
The baseball table and U.S. regional map turn rank outputs into decision-facing displays.
The adjusted versus unadjusted top-ten table supports the stability comparison.
The noise test displays changed rows, overlapping color-coded marks, and a limited rank comparison.
The original coach records permit partial reconciliation of the twelve-factor input table.
The modified rows expose that timeline and gender operations change wins, games, and winning rate.
The continuation preserves transformations for the remaining coaches.
